claims.body: Since 2023-24, Vladař has been a wall against the Oilers, well above his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Don’t be surprised if the Oilers finally get to him.

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 30% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 7th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 39%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Rasmus Ristolainen is out and has missed the last 5 games. Jamie Drysdale has taken his spot beside Travis Sanheim. That pair has had 57% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 72:29 together, up from 23% with Ristolainen.
Nikita Grebenkin is out at least four months (back surgery) and has not played this season. Sean Couturier has taken his spot beside Owen Tippett and Trevor Zegras.
David Jiříček has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 43% of the team’s power-play time in 9 games, up from 2% last season.

Zach Hyman is on injured reserve (neck injury) and has missed the last 5 games. He is a top-six forward. Colton Dach has taken his spot beside Ryan Nugent-Hopkins and Kasperi Kapanen. That line has had 59% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 46:04 together.

Matt Savoie is on long-term injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has not played this season. Leon Draisaitl has taken his spot beside Connor McDavid and Vasily Podkolzin. That line has had 63% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 201:12 together.
Matt Tomkins was added to the roster on Oct 24.
Kasperi Kapanen has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 52% of the team’s power-play time in 17 games, up from 6% last season.
Ty Emberson is no longer killing penalties: 4% of the team’s shorthanded time in 13 games, down from 30% last season.

EDM.head: The Oilers have a lot going for them
EDM.body: Even though Edmonton will be without Hyman, the Oilers have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. The Flyers can make it interesting if their power play gets going.

story.head: Who’s in net for the Oilers?
paras: The Flyers (4-10-4) lost 3-2 to the Rangers on Thursday, and the Oilers (11-3-3) lost 5-4 to Anaheim the same night. Going in, the Flyers are last in the Metropolitan (tied for 28th in the NHL) and the Oilers first in the Pacific (tied for third).

The Flyers haven’t played well, but their record (.333) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .387, and their finishing has held them back. The Oilers’ record (.735) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.591), largely thanks to their finishing.

The Flyers get a lot of their shots blocked (30th). They also block more shots than almost anyone (3rd), and the Oilers’ knack for getting shots through meets a team that blocks a lot. Philadelphia has scored 2.17 goals a game, the fewest in the league. As for the Oilers, they lean on their stars more than any team in the league (lowest), have one of the league’s most dangerous power plays (2nd) and get their defensemen shooting (3rd). Edmonton has scored 4.12 goals a game, the most in the league. Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, especially the Flyers (2nd lowest), so expect a tight one.

Trevor Zegras (4 G / 10 A / 14 P in 18 GP) leads the Flyers in scoring, and Matvei Michkov (10 G / 3 A / 13 P in 18 GP) has a team-high ten goals, tied for tenth in the NHL. Connor McDavid (10 G / 34 A / 44 P in 17 GP) leads the Oilers and the whole NHL in scoring, with ten points in his last five games. Leon Draisaitl (14 G / 17 A / 31 P in 17 GP) has a team-high 14 goals, second in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games.

Dan Vladař (3-4-2 / .883 SV% in 9 GS) will likely start for Philadelphia, and Matt Tomkins (1-1-0 / .878 SV% in 2 GS) for Edmonton. Vladař has a .927 save percentage in six starts against the Oilers, well above his usual .895. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
